conclusion.justification: The report explicitly concludes that evidence from systematic reviews and randomized controlled trials supports the claim, stating that an additional HIV self-testing offer increases HIV-test uptake.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: No—the proposed answer is not supported by the stronger evidence.** Offering HIV self-testing (HIVST) *in addition to* usual/standard testing options generally causes more people to test, particularly when free kits are directly provided or delivered.

The best evidence is systematic reviews and meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials (RCTs). A 2021 review of RCTs in the general population found that testing uptake increased across a range of HIVST delivery and support models; it also found positivity and linkage rates broadly similar to standard testing. https://www.thelancet.com/journals/eclinm/article/PIIS2589-5370(21)00271-6/fulltext

For key populations, a meta-analysis of 10 RCTs concluded that distributing free HIVST kits increased HIV-test uptake versus standard care, including across subgroup analyses. https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s12916-020-01835-z

Individual trials align with that conclusion: the SELPHI randomized trial found regular free kits significantly increased testing frequency among sexually active men who have sex with men. However, more testing did **not** produce faster HIV diagnosis or linkage to care in that study—an important distinction between increasing testing and improving every downstream outcome. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11801452/

There are null findings in the supplied results: one RCT reported testing rose substantially in both arms with no between-arm difference (p=0.85). But that result concerns a broader intervention for young Black participants, not clearly a clean comparison of an added self-test offer versus otherwise identical care. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7882213/

Thus, results can vary by population and delivery method, but the randomized evidence synthesis supports **yes: an additional HIVST offer increases HIV-test uptake**.
